fixes.explanation: Careful, friend, the verse goes the other way. Romans 12:10 says, "Outdo yourselves in honoring one another." Nobody is told to wait for their turn at the honor. The honoring starts with them.
That's right. Romans 12:10 says, "Outdo yourselves in honoring one another." Nobody waits to be honored first. They try to beat each other to the honoring, friend.

Silence isn't the word here, friend. Paul, the apostle writing to Rome, says in Romans 12:12, "Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer." He asks them to keep at prayer, and the word for hard times is patient.

That's the one. Romans 12:14 says, "Bless those who persecute you." I know, friend. I bet it's not the first thing anybody wants to do. But there it is in black and white, and the very next line adds, "Bless and do not curse."

You got it, baker. Romans 12:15 says, "Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep." The word is WITH. When a friend is celebrating, you celebrate. When a friend is crying, you cry with them.

Sometimes that's kind, but it isn't what this verse says. Romans 12:15 says, "Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep." The word is WITH, friend. Paul wants the believers to rejoice and weep along with the person.

Careful, friend, the verse points a different way. Romans 12:16 says, "Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited." Paul isn't telling them to stick close to the important people. He points them toward the lowly.

That's right. Romans 12:16 says, "Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited." Paul doesn't tell them to stick close to the important people. He points them toward the lowly instead, friend.

That's right. Romans 12:18 says, "If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone." The verse speaks only of what's possible on their part, friend. It doesn't make peace depend on how the other person acts.

It really does say it, friend. Romans 12:20 says, "If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink." I bet that one's a surprise to read, but it's right there in the verse. That's what it tells them to do.

That's the one, baker! Romans 12:21 says, "Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good." Notice Paul doesn't say to answer evil with more evil. He says to overcome it with good. I think that's a mic drop of a last line.
